assessment_rule: Promising means that the program has an exact full-Collatz completion gate, substantial closed leverage, or a finite independently checkable certificate target. The bands are organizational judgments, not claims of community consensus or probabilities of success.

approaches.name: Finite residue-cylinder descent certificates
approaches.why_promising: A successful cover is finite, exact, and independently checkable; classical parity cylinders, modular hitting sets, and large verified ranges provide concrete pruning tools.
approaches.hard_boundary: No theorem says that a finite universal cover exists, and long stopping-time examples defeat any unjustified shallow-depth assumption. The gate is stronger than Collatz.

approaches.name: Proof-producing string-rewrite termination
approaches.why_promising: Ten-rule termination is already proved, and modern termination tools can emit finite certificates; the remaining obligation is sharply localized to one exceptional rule relative to the terminating subsystem.
approaches.hard_boundary: After exact normalization, exceptional macrosteps are the accelerated Collatz map. Relative termination is therefore equivalent to Collatz unless a genuinely new global rank or transition invariant is found.

approaches.name: Same-orbit synchronization and carry rigidity
approaches.why_promising: This is the most developed internal program: exact affine dualities, certified finite sectors, cross-depth return constraints, a fixed dual-tail companion with opposite reciprocal-mass behavior, and strong cycle-complexity reductions expose the two remaining obstruction types separately.
approaches.hard_boundary: Every successful local or fixed-window surrogate has countermodels. The active divergence subproblem OPEN-HSCI-SYNC-SHELL-01 must prove a summable bound for the nonpositive rounding-defect mass of the synchronized real companion; local floor-or-ceiling exact edges do not assemble into a long integer shadow. On the cycle side, strict positive full-boundary winding is a q=1-sensitive sufficient strengthening, but its all-depth sign law remains open.

approaches.name: Stationary inverse-fiber extinction
approaches.why_promising: It converts the full conjecture into one monotone-looking strong-induction target and supplies a finite affine envelope and Bellman decomposition at every fixed depth.
approaches.hard_boundary: The exposed minimizing ancestor moves with depth. Controlling that moving minimum uniformly is exactly equivalent to Collatz; fixed-depth compactness does not close the gate.

approaches.name: q-series conjugacy and polynomiality
approaches.why_promising: The selected q-map has carry-free arithmetic and strict degree descent on every polynomial, while a genuine conjugacy transfers its dynamics exactly to the 2-adic Collatz system.
approaches.hard_boundary: The natural coefficient map is not a conjugacy. Proving that the true conjugacy sends every positive integer to a polynomial is explicitly equivalent to Collatz.

approaches.name: Inverse trees and difference inequalities
approaches.completion_gate: A deterministic uniformization theorem converting inverse-tree density or modular hitting into descent for every starting value.
approaches.why_promising: It produces rigorous global lower bounds, exact modular graph constraints, and computable recurrences that can feed a certificate search or a minimal-counterexample argument.
approaches.hard_boundary: Positive density, even density tending toward one, does not exclude one sparse exceptional orbit. This program is an input until it acquires a uniform completion lemma.

approaches.name: Probabilistic, ergodic, and almost-all drift
approaches.completion_gate: A deterministic exceptional-set elimination theorem that applies to the fixed Collatz dynamics, not merely to a random model or almost every seed.
approaches.why_promising: These results rigorously explain the negative average logarithmic drift and prove extremely strong typical-orbit behavior, suggesting what a global Lyapunov mechanism would need to capture.
approaches.hard_boundary: Measure-zero and logarithmic-density-zero exceptional sets may still contain a divergent orbit or cycle. Random models do not supply the required same-orbit uniformity.

approaches.name: Cycle Diophantine bounds and combinatorics
approaches.why_promising: It has the strongest explicit lower bounds and the richest exact finite exclusions, and reduces a hypothetical cycle to rigid valuation words, divisibility conditions, the exact full-boundary winding coordinate rho-Z=g kappa, and the absolute paired-shadow loss T. R104-R112 close one through four corners and sharpen the terminal-preserving cube to more than (s/O(log s))^1.505 vertices. R113-R114 audit why a tempting parity-centered compression fails, while R115 restores the lost terminal bit in an exact lifted packet container and makes every fixed-corner sector effectively finite.
approaches.hard_boundary: Even total cycle exclusion leaves divergent orbits untouched. Existing word-independent congruence methods collapse to one denominator class. R110 shows that relative translated-lattice data loses the absolute anchor. R113 proves that canonical corner deletion can change terminal endpoint parity, invalidating the fixed next-inverse-bit and centered-filter reductions in R113-R114. R115 identifies the exact lift coordinate, but exactness-only packet contraction also has finite counterexamples. A valid contraction must use FCD color, and the full theorem must still control all weights and the absolute anchored carry.
